The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has been open about the company's intent to launch Starship as rapidly as possible in the future. He has claimed that, in less than a decade, SpaceX will be able to launch Starship more than once every hour. SpaceX recently announced plans to invest as much as $100 billion to build a massive launch site in southern Louisiana to support rapid Starship launches.

articles.headline: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
articles.blurb: Science Corporation's vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, is commercially available in Europe for patients who have lost their sight to an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, but the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases. It recently implanted the chip in a patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. The company's work with PRIMA is part of a broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface. It envisions a future where BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications rather than just being used to control computers.

articles.headline: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
articles.blurb: Anthropic was being bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human scale, so it built an in-house version control system called Scion to support its next stage of growth, and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. It also built and shipped a code review surface, code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. Anthropic averaged about 2,500 code changes merged per day in May. It now merges over 30,000 per day, and the rate of growth isn't expected to slow down anytime soon.

articles.headline: How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models
articles.blurb: There are four types of ambition. Speed gets the same work done in less time. Altitude involves going up in abstraction and considering the outcome rather than the individual task. Depth considers a task the way a field-leading expert would, going one level deeper and touching the underlying data, tools, and problems. Range draws on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface using knowledge, tools, and techniques you normally wouldn't.

articles.headline: Were we blue-collar workers all along?

Software developers have tried to separate themselves from this category, but they also make or fix stuff, just in bits rather than atoms. Just like electricians or carpenters, software developers must spend years practicing their craft in order to become skilled and sought-after. Just like anyone else in a skilled trade, software engineers can be outpaced by technology.

articles.headline: ARR vs GAAP Revenue | Spotting “ARR” Lies
articles.blurb: Businesses need to stay honest about what ARR actually is. If ARR doesn't ultimately lead to revenue and cash, then it's a fake metric. Most companies need to redefine or evolve their definitions of ARR for the AI era. ARR should turn into GAAP revenue, and it shouldn't take a really long time for that to happen.

It also distinguishes posts that attract new people from posts that build trust or encourage a purchase. That gives teams a clearer way to judge results: a post meant to introduce the company should not be assessed only by immediate sales. Interested followers can then move into email or a community for a longer relationship.

articles.headline: Capital Stacks For Atoms
articles.blurb: Capital allocation has shifted from bits-based businesses to atoms-based businesses over the last few years. Investors have been directing capital to overcome the physical-world bottlenecks of inference. There's an emerging cohort of atoms-based companies in the fields of energy, manufacturing, space, robotics, and beyond. These hard asset businesses are increasingly built and valued on bundles of cash flows rather than revenue multiples. This requires an entirely different approach to capital formation across the company lifecycle.

articles.headline: OK, I might have been wrong about building with a lean team in the age of AI
articles.blurb: Chatbase is now at 40 people, and it plans to double its number of employees in the next 6 months. Building is now much easier, and the opportunity cost of not building more is huge. Companies that want to build more, grow more, and achieve more still need to hire because humans are still needed in many parts of the building loop. While this might change, it doesn't make sense to act like it isn't true right now.

Its training pipeline filtered 200,000 candidate examples down to about 145,000, using a judge calibrated against 500 manually reviewed merges. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.

articles.headline: Show AI influencers with real people
articles.blurb: AI influencers are seen as less trustworthy because they can't actually use the products they promote. Showing them in everyday moments with real people, like grabbing coffee or going for a run, helps close that gap. In a study of 9,500+ posts and 4 experiments, these scenes drove 20.7% more engagement and made people up to 17.5% more likely to choose the product.

articles.headline: How to spot and fix crappy case studies
articles.blurb: B2B case studies often underperform because they document completed projects instead of telling compelling customer stories. Audit your last 3 by checking whether they explain the customer's original problem. If the stories feel interchangeable, interview a customer stakeholder for 30 mins to uncover what went wrong and what improved. 3-5 distinctive case studies can be more persuasive than 20 generic ones. Use anonymous stories when needed and repurpose them across newsletters and social media.

After posting just 43 times in the past year and seeing newsletter growth stall, Chenell plans to post daily across LinkedIn and other social platforms to test whether social can become a reliable growth channel again.

articles.headline: What Doesn't Get Cheaper
articles.blurb: AI is making websites cheap enough to build for short-term experiments and one-off events that previously weren't worth the cost. However, enterprise websites still require complex integrations. AI can automate production and support decision-making but cannot eliminate the human effort needed to align stakeholders. Generative tools also create collaboration challenges when multiple companies need to edit the same work. As production costs fall, experimentation will expand while complex projects remain expensive because coordination still requires people.

articles.headline: What Pokemon Pokopia Taught Me About the Future of Marketing
articles.blurb: Creativity comes from experimenting and adapting rather than simply generating a finished result. As AI makes content production faster, marketers risk losing the problem-solving and creative judgment that come from hands-on work. A study in 2024 found AI-assisted stories were rated as more creative but also more similar to one another. To stand out, teams should automate repetitive tasks while protecting time for play and experimentation to develop distinctive taste.

articles.headline: Shopping is part of the product
articles.blurb: AI is changing e-commerce discovery by presenting shoppers with product shortlists instead of sending them to search results. A study on AI Mode found that 74% of participants chose the top-ranked product, while only 10% chose a product ranked third or lower. The author outlines a five-stage organic growth loop: earn AI recommendations through product feeds and third-party signals, convert visitors with tools such as quizzes, encourage user-generated content through packaging and product experiences, generate repeat purchases through customer relationships, and build brand recall. Shopping infrastructure and marketing automation are increasingly table stakes, while customer relationships, creator partnerships, community, first-party data, and brand recall create longer-term advantages.

articles.blurb: Binance rolled out its AI-powered trading interface to all global English-language users on October 12, following a beta that drew 150,000 participants over five weeks beginning September 7. The free suite includes AI-generated portfolio summaries, top-mover analysis, voice alerts, on-demand market briefings in text or audio, and a generative UI that adapts displayed market data and tools to each user's stated interests and experience level. The launch extends Binance's super-app strategy, using AI as an onboarding and retention layer for traders who lack the background to interpret raw market data. Additional language support is currently rolling out.

articles.headline: Informed Diffusion: making home builders publish fast
articles.blurb: Informed Diffusion is a four-tier gossip protocol that cuts home-builder payload delivery from 6.3 seconds to 0.63 seconds P99, matching and surpassing the 1.8-second benchmark datacenter builders achieve on mixed-bandwidth networks. Pipelining, push/pull chunk announcement, erasure coding, and neighbor-aware scheduling via per-payload HAVE bitmaps reduce bandwidth utilization from 4.4 to 1.7 payload copies and hold delivery under the 3-second budget against 50% withholding nodes, 10 Mbps throttled uplinks, and payloads ranging from 128 KiB to 2 MiB. The sole wire protocol addition is HAVE bitmaps carried in existing gossipsub control messages, with all other improvements left to local client implementation, allowing adoption without mesh topology changes or new topics.

articles.headline: NFT marketplace Blur is shutting down after volumes collapse 99%
articles.blurb: Blur will close its marketplace and lending arm Blend on November 12 after monthly Ethereum NFT trading volume fell 99.5% from its March 2023 peak of $1.43 billion, when the platform held over 70% of ETH NFT market share, to under $7 million. Token Terminal records zero protocol revenue across three years of operation, as Blur charged no transaction fees throughout its run, a model that built dominant volume but left no economic foundation. The shutdown follows Blast network's closure by ten days, with both projects built by Tieshun Roquerre (Pacman), and Blast's TVL having fallen from $2 billion to roughly $32 million before its team cited unsustainable operational costs. The BLUR token dropped over 20% on the announcement, trading around $0.015.

articles.headline: The Death of the Interface
articles.blurb: David Marcus, who led Meta's M assistant and Libra and now runs Lightspark, argues that AI models and stablecoin law have finally arrived together, so apps, websites, and buttons will give way to agents you simply talk to. Payments today assume a human in the loop (checkout pages, texted codes, fraud, and dispute flows), so money must stop moving through a UI. Stablecoins are no longer a standalone category. To be useful, they need fast settlement networks, embedded wallets, fiat connectivity, and card networks, which he calls “headless money,” a simple API that agents can use to move value anywhere, 24/7, with revocable spending limits and clear liability for mistakes. A few payment-stack companies will be worth hundreds of billions, but the companies running the winning agents will earn far more, since payment stacks earn only 1 to 300 basis points.

articles.headline: Crypto Trader 'Realist' Reports Knifepoint Robbery at UK Home
articles.blurb: UK-based crypto trader 'Realist' reported a knifepoint home robbery valued at approximately $800,000, with on-chain records corroborating the claim via 719,000 USDC transferred through an identified Solana address. The incident extends a documented pattern of physical attacks targeting traders whose wallet balances and identities are linkable onchain. Attackers use blockchain transparency to identify high-value targets, then coerce asset transfers through physical force rather than technical exploits. This attack category, sometimes called a "$5 wrench attack," bypasses cryptographic security and poses a growing physical threat to high-net-worth on-chain participants.

Morpho's deployment on the chain has drawn approximately $1.1 billion in deposits, demonstrating that DeFi lending primitives can attract meaningful TVL when layered on top of tokenized equity infrastructure. The combined metrics, trading volume plus onchain credit demand, suggest users are treating tokenized stocks as composable collateral rather than purely buy-and-hold instruments.

articles.headline: No Room for Bugs

Tools that rely on separate models risk implementation drift, where the model no longer matches the actual code. Hydro addresses this limitation by running correctness checks directly against deployed code.
